ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Marcus Aurelius Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for chronic epigastric and lower chest pain after meals, poor appetite and poor sleep: cardiac assessment first, review of an opium-containing remedy, and gastroenterology referral for endoscopy. Concerns: He has had pain in his chest and stomach after meals for more than a year and wants to know whether his heart is sound; He sleeps badly and is tired, and must stay clear-headed for his work; He has taken the herbal paste for years and does not want to be judged for it, or made to stop it before he is ready. [S]

tr.td: Opium-containing compounded herbal paste (an electuary of honey, many herbs and poppy, from an overseas supplier; not prescribed and not regulated, so its morphine content is unknown), about a pea-sized amount (roughly 0.5 g) by mouth at bedtime most nights for about six years, and now and then in the morning before a long day
About 0.5 g at bedtime most nights; occasionally a second amount in the morning
Calcium carbonate 500 mg chewable tablet, one or two tablets as needed for heartburn, no more than six a day, until the endoscopy
One or two tablets as needed, at least four hours apart; no more than six a day
Polyethylene glycol 3350 powder, 17 g dissolved in a glass of water by mouth once daily as needed for constipation
Naloxone 4 mg nasal spray, one spray into one nostril for suspected opioid overdose, repeated in 2 to 3 minutes in the other nostril if there is no response; call 911
One spray for suspected overdose; repeat every 2 to 3 minutes if needed
Omeprazole 20 mg delayed-release capsule, one capsule by mouth 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for eight weeks, for erosive esophagitis
One capsule each morning before breakfast for eight weeks
Omeprazole 20 mg delayed-release capsule, one capsule by mouth before breakfast on days after heartburn returns (on-demand therapy after the eight-week course)
One capsule on a day with heartburn; no more than one a day
Opium-containing compounded herbal paste (unregulated, strength unknown), about 0.5 g by mouth at bedtime on alternate nights, a reduction he chose and made himself
About 0.5 g at bedtime every other night
Opium-containing compounded herbal paste (unregulated, strength unknown), a smaller amount, about 0.3 g, by mouth at bedtime on about two nights a week, a further reduction he chose
About 0.3 g at bedtime on about two nights a week
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, one or two tablets by mouth every six hours as needed for fever or aches, no more than 3 g a day
One or two tablets every six hours as needed; no more than six a day

tr.td: New patient visit for chronic epigastric and lower chest pain after meals, poor appetite and poor sleep: cardiac assessment first, review of an opium-containing remedy, and gastroenterology referral for endoscopy
Gastroenterology consultation with upper endoscopy and biopsy, review of the CT coronary angiogram, diagnosis of erosive esophagitis, and start of omeprazole
Five-week review: reflux symptoms on omeprazole, biopsy results, sleep therapy, and the remedy
Fifteen-week review after the eight-week omeprazole course: on-demand therapy, sleep, the remedy, and mood
Same-day sick visit for mild COVID-19 while taking an opium-containing remedy

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Cardiac assessment first: twelve-lead ECG today; a structured estimate of the chance of coronary disease; no troponin, because the pain is chronic and there is no acute episode; CT coronary angiography within a week, chosen over stress testing because it excludes both obstructive and non-obstructive plaque and informs the cholesterol decision; call 911 for chest pain at rest lasting more than a few minutes, or pain with breathlessness, sweating or fainting

Gastroenterology consultation for upper endoscopy within one week, with gastric biopsies for Helicobacter pylori, to find the cause of the chest and epigastric pain after the cardiac assessment and to advise on treatment; no acid-suppressing drug before the endoscopy, with an antacid as needed

Respectful review of the opium-containing remedy: what it is, why he takes it, and what it does for him; a DSM-5-TR assessment; a prescription drug monitoring program check; a urine drug test with his consent, explained as part of care; naloxone at home; no alcohol, sleep medicines or other sedatives on the same night; never more than his usual amount; stored closed and out of reach; how opioids slow the gut; no forced or abrupt taper, and any reduction his own choice, made slowly; reviewed at every visit, with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

Chronic insomnia: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) with the clinic's behavioral sleep clinician, six sessions, with a sleep diary, sleep restriction, stimulus control and work on racing thoughts at night; Insomnia Severity Index at intake and at each review; no hypnotic or sedating antihistamine, which would add to the opioid

Strain of command and mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at follow-up; protected time for meals and sleep, decisions delegated after a set hour, and his evening writing kept; counselling if scores rise
Constipation: polyethylene glycol as needed, fluids and fiber; review as the remedy changes

Reflux esophagitis: omeprazole 20 mg 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for eight weeks, then a trial off with omeprazole on demand; the evening meal at least three hours before lying down, the head of the bed raised, and less wine at night; no repeat endoscopy for grade B esophagitis; esophageal manometry and reflux monitoring off therapy if symptoms persist or swallowing becomes difficult

Mild COVID-19: rest, fluids and acetaminophen; honey for cough; no codeine or dextromethorphan cough medicine, sedating antihistamine or sleep aid while he takes the opium-containing remedy, and no more of the remedy than usual; naloxone at hand; antiviral treatment offered and declined after a shared decision; stay away from others until fever-free for 24 hours without medicine and improving, then added precautions for five days; call 911 for breathlessness, chest pain, confusion or blue lips, and return for oxygen saturation below 94% on a home oximeter

Colorectal cancer screening: colonoscopy ordered for the first quiet stretch of his assignment, with a split-dose bowel preparation and two extra days of polyethylene glycol beforehand because the opioid slows the bowel, and no remedy the night before; fecal immunochemical testing each year if he prefers not to have colonoscopy
A cardiac cause of the chest pain excluded within two weeks
Normal ECG at intake; CT coronary angiography one week later: calcium score 0 and no plaque
Chest and stomach pain after meals controlled, with appetite and weight returning
Pain gone on omeprazole; occasional mild heartburn after late meals on on-demand therapy; weight up 2 kg
Insomnia Severity Index below 8 within four months
Insomnia Severity Index 7 after six sessions of CBT-I
The remedy used as safely as he can: naloxone at home, never with alcohol or sleep medicines, and decisions about it his own
Naloxone at home; no alcohol on nights he takes it; by his own choice now about two nights a week
